newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $1-$1.50 down, Brent 5-10 cts up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $1-$1.50 down, Brent 5-10 cts up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures should open $1.00-$1.50 a tonne lower on Wednesday playing catch-up to Tuesday's late reversal on crude and NYMEX heating oil but Brent is expected to open firmer after the release of U.S. inventory data, brokers said.
IPE June gas oil settled at $177.75 a tonne, extending its discount to July by 50 cents. July Brent closed at $20.00 a barrel, down 12 cents.
"Gas oil was due $2 down but Brent is a bit firmer in Singapore and the stocks figures were neutral to slightly bullish so it probably won't make that," said a broker.

July Brent on Singapore's SIMEX was trading 10 cents firmer at $20.10 a barrel by 0800 GMT on Wednesday, helped by gains on NYMEX crude overnight after the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported a big fall in inventories last week.
API data showed crude stocks fell by 5.9 million barrels as refinery throughputs were ratcheted up to 97.6 percent, the highest level for this time of year in at least four years.
Middle distillate and gasoline showed modest stocks builds of 1.9 million and 837,000 barrels, respectively.
"There's been a big jump in capacity in the last two weeks and yet the product builds have not been huge," said a broker.
"That means usage must be running quite high which must be supportive."
But others said the unexpected step up in refinery utilization would begin to exert pressure on products, in turn squeezing crack spreads and margins still further.
"I think this market has done enough on the upside for the time being," said a broker.
Several European refineries are considering crude throughput cut as returns dip into the red for less complex plants and hover near loss-making levels for those with upgrading capacity.
